name: Medellín
tagline: The City of Eternal Spring, once notorious, now a hillside metropolis of cable cars, street art, Botero sculptures, cafés and hopeful energy.
highlight: Riding the Metrocable up to the hillside neighbourhoods, with the whole valley spread out below.
shortDescription: Colombia's innovation city, with Comuna 13's street art and escalators, Plaza Botero, Metrocable rides, Parque Arví, El Poblado's restaurants and a mild climate all year.
metaDescription: A Medellín travel guide: Comuna 13, Plaza Botero, Metrocable, Parque Arví, El Poblado, bandeja paisa, coffee, safety, where to stay and a three-day plan.
goodFor: Cities, nightlife, food, street art, digital nomads

intro: Medellín, in the Aburrá Valley of the Andes at about 1,500 metres, is Colombia's second city, home to about 2.5 million people. It is nicknamed the City of Eternal Spring for its mild climate, with daytime temperatures around 25°C for most of the year. In the 1980s and early 1990s the city was known as the base of the Medellín Cartel and among the most violent in the world. Since then, it has transformed, through investment in public transport, libraries and parks in poorer neighbourhoods, and has won awards as one of the world's most innovative cities.

The best symbol is the Metrocable, a cable car network connected to the metro that links hillside barrios to the city, and the outdoor escalators of Comuna 13, once one of the most dangerous areas, now a hub of street art, hip-hop and tours led by residents. In the centre, Plaza Botero displays 23 bronze sculptures by Medellín-born Fernando Botero, and the Museum of Antioquia holds more of his works.

The city is also a comfortable base: El Poblado and Laureles have restaurants, cafés and nightlife, Parque Arví offers nature on the edge of the city, and Guatapé and coffee farms are within easy day trips. Three days is ideal, and visitors should be alert to safety, especially with drinks and strangers, and avoid the cartel-era tourism that glorifies violence.

whyVisit.intro: Medellín is a pleasant, dynamic city that shows how much Colombia has changed.
